citation.authors: Okoro EO, Ogunbiyi AO, George AO, Subulade MO

cited_by.title: Does diet cause acne? Sugar, dairy and foods linked to spots

record.population: 464 adolescents (mean age 13.6) in schools in Ibadan, southwest Nigeria; 64.4% had acne
record.design: Cross-sectional survey with examination for facial acne and food-frequency questions
record.finding: Acne was more common in students who reported at least daily milk as a drink (72.6% vs 62.0%), corn (76.6% vs 62.3%), fried beef (75.0% vs 62.1%) and cake (77.8% vs 62.3%), and less common with daily bananas (55.3% vs 67.6%). The authors say an interventional dietary study is needed.
record.note: A cross-sectional snapshot: it cannot show that food caused acne. Funding not checked.
